unit_note: Measurements shown as metric / US imperial. Temperatures shown as °C / °F. 1 cup = 240ml, 1 tbsp = 15ml, 1 tsp = 5ml, 1 fl oz = 30ml, 1 oz = 28g.

recipes.title: Ginger Bug
recipes.summary: A wild starter culture made from fresh ginger, sugar, and water. The natural yeast and bacteria living on ginger skin kick off fermentation, giving you a live base that carbonates any sweetened drink.
steps: Day 1: combine 4 cups (1L) filtered water, 2 tbsp (30ml) chopped ginger, and 2 tbsp (30ml / 25g) sugar in a clean jar. Stir to dissolve and cover loosely.
Days 2-7: each day, stir in 1 tbsp (15ml) fresh ginger and 1 tbsp (15ml / 12g) sugar, then re-cover.
It's ready when stirring brings up small bubbles (usually days 3-4) and it smells yeasty with a lightly sour, fizzy taste.
To use: strain out the old ginger and set aside 200ml (¾ cup) for a soda batch, then top the jar back up to 1L (4¼ cups) with water and feed 1 tbsp of each.
To rest it: keep in the fridge and feed 1 tbsp of each once a week. To wake it: feed and leave at room temperature 12-24 hours before using.
recipes.warning_signs: Fuzzy mold (white, green, black, or pink) or a rotten smell means throw it out. A thin white film or cloudy liquid is normal.

soda.title: Ginger Bug Soda
steps: Boil 1L (4¼ cups) water, then add the ginger, sugar, lemon peel, and spices. Simmer 5 minutes and let it cool to room temperature.
Strain the ginger bug and measure out 200ml (¾ cup); feed the rest.
Strain the cooled liquid into a pitcher and discard the solids. Add the remaining 2L (8½ cups) water and the lemon juice.
Stir in the ginger bug liquid, pour into 4 x 700ml (3-cup) bottles leaving 1 inch (2.5cm) headspace, and seal tightly.
Let it carbonate 2-3 days, opening briefly to check the fizz.

recipes.title: Ginger Beer
recipes.summary: A classic spicy ginger ale built from a live ginger bug. Yields 4 x 700ml bottles.
steps: Bring 1L (4¼ cups) water to a boil. Stir in the ginger, sugar, lemon peel, peppercorns, allspice, and cloves until the sugar dissolves. Simmer gently 5 minutes, then remove from heat and cool until just warm.
Strain the ginger bug through a fine mesh and measure out 200ml (¾ cup). Top up the rest with fresh water and feed 1 tbsp (15ml) each of ginger and sugar.
Once the liquid is lukewarm or cooler (heat kills the yeast), strain it into a pitcher and discard the solids. Add the remaining 2L (8½ cups) water and the lemon juice, and stir.
Stir in the 200ml (¾ cup) ginger bug. Pour into 4 x 700ml bottles, leaving 1 inch (2.5cm) headspace, and cap tightly.
Open a cap briefly to check the fizz; give it more days for a stronger sparkle.
recipes.prep_tips: Leave out the lemon and spices for a simpler version. Keeps for a couple of weeks refrigerated, slowly losing sweetness.

recipes.title: Thyme Pink Lemonade
recipes.summary: A sweet-tart pink lemonade with a subtle herb note.
recipes.prep_tips: Blend the berries, lemon juice, and ginger into a purée and strain through a fine sieve so the pour stays clean.

recipes.title: Pineapple Star Anise
recipes.summary: Bright pineapple with a gentle licorice note from star anise.
recipes.prep_tips: Start with one segment of star anise and add more to taste.

recipes.title: Cherry Chili
recipes.summary: Sweet, jammy cherry with a warm, gentle heat from ancho chili.

ingredients.name: Ancho chili
ingredients.amount: ½-1 inch / 12-25mm (or a dash of spice)

recipes.prep_tips: Crush the cherries lightly to free their juice; use a small piece of chili so it warms rather than overpowers.

recipes.title: Raspberry Lemon Ginger
recipes.summary: Tart raspberry, bright lemon, and ginger heat that builds on the finish.
recipes.prep_tips: Mash the berries into a paste to release their flavor; grated ginger adds bite and can boost fizz.

recipes.title: Smoky Citrus
recipes.summary: Bright lime and citrus over a deep smoky tea base.
recipes.prep_tips: Brew the lapsang tea as usual; if the smoke is too strong, cut it with regular black tea.

recipes.title: Mango Tajín
recipes.summary: Juicy mango with a chili-lime-salt kick from Tajín.
recipes.prep_tips: Mash the mango lightly to release more juice for carbonation; start with a small pinch of Tajín.

recipes.title: Hoppy Pineapple
recipes.summary: A sunny, IPA-style brew with tropical citrus and a floral hop bite.
recipes.prep_tips: Add the hops directly and taste after 4-6 hours, then remove. For more intensity, steep the hops in warm (not boiling) water 5-10 minutes, cool, and add.

recipes.title: Blue Spirulina Coconut
recipes.summary: Coconut water and ginger with vivid blue spirulina for a striking color.

ingredients.name: Ginger simple syrup (or sugar + ginger juice)

recipes.prep_tips: DIY ginger simple syrup: heat 1 cup (240ml) water with ¾ cup (180ml / 150g) sugar until dissolved, add 225g (8 oz) peeled cubed ginger, simmer 15 minutes, then steep 60-90 minutes off heat. Strain and refrigerate (makes about 1 cup). With a juicer, swap the syrup for ½ tsp fresh ginger juice.
